### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-webhooks`, `@objectstack/service-messaging`, touching **44** documentable anchor(s).

**47** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57c51aab4d2f63293676e9412daed8a5fc54c1bc`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `logError (6 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 48 pages)`
- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **7** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57c51aab4d2f63293676e9412daed8a5fc54c1bc` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1ab02816399185c40801f5733f43c0dc5d5392d5` — the merge of head `b4a2146cb6c24b77a6a5244274195b2067e295b1` into base `57c51aab4d2f63293676e9412daed8a5fc54c1bc`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1ab02816399185c40801f5733f43c0dc5d5392d5 && git checkout 1ab02816399185c40801f5733f43c0dc5d5392d5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 57c51aab4d2f63293676e9412daed8a5fc54c1bc b4a2146cb6c24b77a6a5244274195b2067e295b1 && git checkout -B drift-repro 57c51aab4d2f63293676e9412daed8a5fc54c1bc && git merge --no-ff b4a2146cb6c24b77a6a5244274195b2067e295b1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57c51aab4d2f63293676e9412daed8a5fc54c1bc
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 57c51aab4d2f63293676e9412daed8a5fc54c1bc` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

declaration and the docs claim, not reviewed as code)

Inputs: PR #27474 body and file list, the net diff against `main` at the merge-base 9462d8ad, the 50 check-runs on this head (37 success, 13 skipped, 0 failure; the ten required contexts are all `success`), and the dev's open question quoted in the brief. No card by design (maintainer disclosure ruling); the PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies, named right or wrong against the cited code:

1. **The new `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` on both door faces — right.** Both faces run the one body `serveRedeliver` (`registerAdminRoutes` hands it the Hono context; the `webhooks` slot's `handleRedeliver` hands it `requestDoorContext(request)`), and the new gate sits in that body after the ADR-0069 gate and the `401`, before `c.req.json()`. The refusal is one of three module constants, so the body cannot carry a delivery id, subscription id or webhook name; `webhook-redeliver-entitlement.test.ts` pins one identical body across seven request shapes on each face, `redeliverHttp` never called, every row left `dead`. The runtime dispatcher domain (`packages/runtime/src/domains/webhooks.ts`) forwards the request unread and adds no rule, so the hosted face inherits the gate by construction.
2. **The new `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` — right in direction, new in reach.** `tryGetService(ctx, ['security'])` treats a throwing lookup as absent, and `judgeRedeliverEntitlement` answers `NO_DECIDER` (503, remedy in the message) for no service or one without `explain`, and `UNDECIDED` (503, cause at `error`) when the resolution or the decision throws. That is the AGENTS.md direction (prefer failing to falling back). Every composition the repo ships registers `security` before the door is reached: `os serve` composes `SecurityPlugin` on every boot (`@objectstack/cli` depends on `@objectstack/plugin-security`, so its optional dynamic import succeeds), and the verify harness, `plugin-dev` and the schema-migration plugin set compose it too; `webhooks` is loaded as a capability provider on the same boot. The 503 therefore reaches only a hand-built kernel. See ④ for the one thing missing around it (loudness at boot).
3. **The API-key face — unchanged, right.** The door never admitted a key (`webhook-redeliver-api-key.pin.test.ts`, untouched and green: a key-only request reads no session and is `401` before the gate), and the gate itself is composed with `credentials: 'session-only'`, so `resolveAuthzContext` is handed no headers for the key arm. Nothing new is accepted.
4. **The organization scoping — right in sequence, wrong in one input.** The gate and the replay read the same session once (`resolveSession`), and `activeOrganizationId` is threaded into both; the in-process-session-read pin still holds at one read because the composition is fed `session: { established }` and never calls `getSession` again. An entitled caller keeps `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` outside the active organization. But the composition is handed `tenancy: undefined`, so the session arm's organization vetting is not applied here as every other posture-reading door applies it — ④ must-fix.
5. **The `409` veto ordering — unchanged, right.** The entitlement gate runs before the body is read, so an unentitled caller never reaches `assertHttpRedeliverable` or the installed guard; an entitled caller keeps `DELIVERY_NOT_ELIGIBLE` and `DELIVERY_NEVER_SENT` as `409`. The control case (administrator still answered `409` with the subscription name) pins that the gate hides nothing from an administrator.
6. **The ADR-0069 held session — unchanged, right.** `evaluateAuthGate(session?.user, '')` is still asked first, so a held session is answered the gate's own `403` and the entitlement is never asked; the gate is composed with `authGate: 'withhold'`, so it is not decided twice. The anonymous case pins that the security double is never asked below a `401`.
7. **The entitlement itself — right against the shipped sets.** `sys_webhook` is `managedBy: 'config'`, so the registry-driven managed-write denies (the `better-auth` bucket) do not touch it, and the object declares no capability requirement; `admin_full_access`, `organization_admin` and `organization_admin_no_bypass` carry `allowEdit` through their `objects['*']` wildcard, `member_default` names no `sys_webhook` entry. `ISecurityService.explain` answers the object-level question as `!capsDeny && crudAllowed && !denyAll && !delegatorMissing` on the same evaluator and RLS compiler enforcement uses; the self-explain branch runs on the request's own context. The docs' sentence "the shipped administrator sets carry it; a member baseline does not" holds.
8. **The published posture statements — mostly updated, with residue.** `webhooks.mdx` section 8, the checklist clause text, the dogfood authz matrix row and the `http-delivery.object.ts` comment now state the gate. Three places at this head still state the retired posture: `packages/services/service-messaging/src/http-outbox.ts` line 268 and `sql-http-outbox.ts` line 477 (both "served to any authenticated user"), and the checklist clause's own `verify` field (line 648, "the no-capability posture ... in the route's own docblock", a docblock that no longer says that). Should-fix, ④.

### ② Semver level

- **`patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-webhooks` — right for the level.** `Metadata-protocol: none` is true (no key, value or metadata type an author writes changes), and by the Post-Task Checklist a non-protocol change ships `patch` whatever its direction. No other released package's published surface moves: `http-delivery.object.ts` changes a comment only; the `http-conformance` and `dogfood` edits are test fixtures and a matrix row.
- **The `Clause-②: no` line should carry the `(narrowing)` arm — yes.** The question the value answers is whether the card widens an accept set or enlarges a public surface: `no` is true. The arm answers the other fact the value cannot carry: this diff narrows a published accept set of a public door — the set of callers `POST /api/v1/webhooks/redeliver` admits, which the docs published as "any authenticated user", the platform checklist pinned as the designed posture, and the dogfood authz matrix recorded as `enforced`. The PR body itself names it so ("this narrows who may call a public door", "deployments that relied on non-administrators pressing redeliver change to 403", with a migration line). That is the definition `clause2-line.mjs` gives the arm (`no (narrowing)`: not a widening, but breaking), and it is the carrier `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` reads a declared narrowing from. As committed, the absent arm declares no direction, so `reviewFace` reads this tree as the declaration face (`TIER_DEFAULT`), the opposite of what the body says it owes — the tree and the body disagree. Correcting it: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` in the changeset body and the PR body, the `**BREAKING**` banner, exactly one `adr-0087:` disposition marker (the gate prints the closed set), the migration line already present, and the `Skills-docs:` third line the arm owes the PR body. The level stays `patch`. Recorded as a should-fix in ④ because the ruling made the arm optional and an absent arm is a legal reading, not a false one.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Which access governs redelivery (the dev's open question) — ESCALATED to the maintainer, not decided here.** The axis is a human-floor decision. Recommendation, with the reasoning the code supports: **A, `update` on `sys_webhook`** (as implemented). Replaying a delivery resets the `sys_http_delivery` row and sends a signed request to the subscriber: a write-shaped act with an external side effect, the same power as editing or re-activating the subscription. B (`read` on `sys_http_delivery`) is the object the button sits on, but a read-wildcard principal (`viewer_readonly`, or any read-only set) would gain a write-shaped send, and `read` on the delivery log is also what an auditor holds. One consequence of A the maintainer should weigh: an operator persona that may read deliveries but not edit webhooks loses the button; the migration is an `allowEdit` grant on `sys_webhook` through a permission set, which also opens editing the subscription itself. If that coupling is unwanted, the alternative is a dedicated capability on the delivery object, which is a spec change outside this PR.
- **A kernel with no `security` service now answers 503 (the dev's note) — answered: right direction.** Fail closed with a remedy in the message is the rule (prefer failing to falling back); every shipped composition registers `security` (① item 2), so the new behaviour reaches only a hand-built kernel, and the changeset says so. One gap on loudness at boot, ④ should-fix.
- **The organization vetting input — raised here, judged in ④.** The composition the gate uses exists so that no door omits an input another door has; this door omits the tenancy posture.
- **Author:** `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (the relay). No non-fleet login to name.
- **Card:** none, by the maintainer disclosure ruling; this record describes the change the way the PR body does and nothing more.

### ④ Design judgment

Judged against the cited code on `main` at the merge-base and at this head, not against the PR body's account.

**Must-fix (FAIL):**

1. **The gate is composed without the tenancy posture, so its admission is not the data API's on a walled posture.** `judgeRedeliverEntitlement` calls `resolveRequestExecutionContext` with `tenancy: undefined`, with a comment borrowed from the `/auth/me` endpoints ("a session-only door, as the `/auth/me` endpoints are"). The composition's own table says `undefined` is for a door that reads no posture, and `/auth/me` qualifies because it writes nothing tenant-scoped. This door does: it threads the session's `activeOrganizationId` into a write on a tenant-scoped object (the tenant threading the door's docblock records). With no posture, `resolveAuthzContext`'s session arm (`vetOrganizationClaim`) lets the stored organization claim stand as made, so the caller's grants, positions and the context's `tenantId` are resolved in the claimed organization; the dispatcher and REST hand the composition their `tenancy` resolver, so for the same session the data API's write gate drops a claim no current membership backs and resolves the caller with no active organization, where the `isolated` tenant layer composes to deny-all. The two admissions therefore differ for a session whose membership in the claimed organization has ended, exactly the per-request check the maintainer ruling of 2026-09-05 (option B, recorded in the session arm's own comment) put on every door, and the gate's stated equivalence ("the same admission the data API's write gate gives that caller", "cannot disagree") does not hold on `isolated` or `group`. The change is still strictly narrower than `main` (which admitted every signed-in session and threaded the same unvetted claim), so this is a hardening that stops short of its claim, not a regression. Fix, in the gate: hand the composition the door's own resolver (a `tenancy` thunk that reads the kernel's `tenancy` service, through the same `tryGetService` discipline; `classifyAdmissionTenancyPosture` already answers a never-registered service quietly and a failed one as `AuthzStoreUnavailableError`, which the gate's `catch` turns into the 503 it already has), and then thread the vetted `context.tenantId` into the replay rather than the raw session claim, so the organization the replay writes into is the one the caller was admitted in. Pin it: the entitlement suite gains a case on a walled posture where the double's `tenancy` service answers `isolated`, the session names an organization the member list no longer backs, and the door answers the caller-level refusal with nothing replayed. Delta review by this seat on the new head.

**Should-fix:**

2. **Declare the narrowing.** `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` in the changeset and PR body, the `**BREAKING**` banner, one `adr-0087:` disposition marker, and the `Skills-docs:` line; level stays `patch` (② above).
3. **Say the 503 once at boot.** AGENTS.md's "absence must be loud": `bootRedeliverDoor` runs at `kernel:ready`, after every `init`, and already warns when the engine or messaging is missing; when no `security` service is registered it should say once, naming the remedy, that the door is mounted and will answer `503` to every caller. Today the absence is discovered per request in the server log.
4. **Retire the three stale posture statements** named in ① item 8 (`http-outbox.ts` line 268, `sql-http-outbox.ts` line 477, the checklist clause's `verify` field), so no comment or checklist field still describes the door as open to any authenticated user.
5. **Anchor the ADR-0124 D1 site.** The gate is a load-bearing enforcement of D1 and the diff cites it in code; Prime Directive 13 asks for one anchor JSON under `scripts/adr-anchors/` named for `redeliver-entitlement.ts`.

**Held (no finding):** the identity judged is the session the door already read (`session: { established }` carries `user.id` and `session.userId` from that read, and the gate refuses on `context.userId !== input.userId`); an impersonated session resolves as the impersonated user, which is also the identity the door acts as and logs (`requestedBy`); a held session is stopped by the ADR-0069 gate before the entitlement; the refusal body is a constant and the gate runs before any row-dependent branch on both faces, so neither body nor the branch taken distinguishes rows (the cost of the refusal depends on the caller's grant resolution only); the double registered in the amended suites answers only `update` on `sys_webhook`, so those suites cannot pass on a looser question; the engine-double ledger row is recorded.

Implemented-by: `claude/harden-webhook-redeliver-door`
Reviewed-by: `session_017xRBcSwDXZrZg7nGjP6P3U`

**VERDICT: FAIL**
